nodes.name: Co-precipitation of V/Fe PBA
nodes.procedure: V/Fe PBA powder was synthesized by a simple co-precipitation method. Two types of solutions were used for the precipitation: 40×10⁻³ M VCl₂ (Aldrich) and a mixture of 20×10⁻³ M Na₄Fe(CN)₆·10H₂O (Sigma-Aldrich) and 200×10⁻³ M NaCl (Sigma-Aldrich). The two solutions were separately dispersed in 50 mL of DI water added HCl (7 vol%). Both solutions were slowly added dropwise to a 1 vol% HCl aqueous solution with the aid of a pumping machine and vigorous stirring, and the molar ratio of VCl₂ to Na₄Fe(CN)₆ was maintained constant during the co-precipitation process. After complete mixing, the mixture was heated at 60 °C for 3 h. The obtained precipitate powders were filtered and washed with DI water and ethanol several times to remove the residual chemicals. Finally, the V/Fe PBA powders were dried in a vacuum at 80 °C overnight.

nodes.source_text: Galvanostatic charging/discharging was performed under a current density of 110 mA g⁻¹ (≈1.2 C) within a potential range of 0.45 to 1.15 V versus Ag/AgCl... showed a high discharge capacity of 91 mA h g⁻¹... exhibited a capacity of ≈55 mA h g⁻¹ at the end of the cycling (250th cycle)

The average discharge capacities measured with the increase in the current densities of 55, 110, 220, 440, 880, 1760, and 3520 mA g⁻¹ were 94.1, 80.1, 72.9, 67.9, 60.0, 58.3, and 54.0 mA h g⁻¹, respectively. The results... demonstrated... a delivered capacity of 57% was still utilized under... 3520 mA g⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: V/Fe PBA shows aggregated nanoparticles with irregular shapes; co-precipitation (with/without HCl) yields narrower particle size distribution than simple mixing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1A–C shows the surface morphology of V/Fe PBA after the different synthetic procedures. All three methods produced powders with an aggregated form of nanoparticles with irregular shapes.

properties.description: Low magnification SEM showing aggregated nanoparticles
High magnification SEM showing individual nanoparticles

nodes.characterization_summary: All diffraction peaks indexed to cubic phase V3[Fe(CN)6]2 (PDF 00-042-1440); co-precipitation with HCl shows sharpest peaks and highest crystallinity without broad amorphous background.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1D shows the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of V/Fe PBA powder synthesized by co-precipitation (with and without HCl) and simple mixing. All the diffraction peaks were indexed with the cubic phase of V3[Fe(CN)6]2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co-precipitation with HCl shows well-grown crystallites ~tens of nm (red arrows) with amorphous regions (white arrows); simple mixing shows fine nanocrystals in amorphous matrix.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the V/Fe PBAs fabricated by simple mixing, fine nanocrystals with sizes of a few nanometers ... the powders synthesized by the co-precipitation method (with HCl) contained well-grown crystallites a few tens of nanometers in size, as marked by red arrows in Figure 1F.

nodes.characterization_summary: Shows M-C stretching (450-650 cm⁻¹), V=O (980 cm⁻¹), C≡N stretching (2095 cm⁻¹), and broad H2O peak at ~3430 cm⁻¹ confirming PBA structure with vanadyl and water molecules.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spectrum of the V/Fe PBA powder shows M-C (or M-C≡N-M) stretching, V=O, and -C≡N- stretching ... corresponding to wavenumbers of 450–650, 980, and 2095 cm⁻¹, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Confirms adsorbed/ligand water molecules in V/Fe PBA structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FT-IR and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) (bottom of Figure 1G), the chemical formula of the as-synthesized V/Fe PBAs was determined to be Na0.4(VO)3[Fe(CN)6]2·12H2O.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform elemental distribution of Na, V, Fe, C, N, O; atomic ratios Na/V = 0.13, V/Fe = 1.52.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1H presents the EDS mapping images ... From the EDS result, the atomic ratios of Na/V and V/Fe were measured at 0.13 and 1.52, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ Fe and V K-edge XANES show systematic energy shifts confirming V³⁺→V⁴⁺→V⁵⁺ and Fe²⁺→Fe³⁺ redox during charging.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3D depicts the calculated energy as a function of the normalized charge capacity ... charge compensation upon the charging/discharging was occurred by the changes in valance state of V and Fe ions.

nodes.characterization_summary: Charge transfer resistance Rct sharply increases during early cycles and saturates, correlating with capacity fade; Rfilm stable.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 6D. Changes in resistance Re (electrolyte), Rfilm (film), and Rct (charge transfer) with cycle number calculated from the simulation of the Nyquist plots.

nodes.characterization_summary: Dissolved V ions more prominent than Fe (V/Fe ratio 3/2); <1.5% V and <0.6% Fe dissolved after 250 cycles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 6E. Concentration of dissolved V and Fe ions as a function of the cycle number measured by ICP-OES.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cycled cathodes at 50th, 100th, 250th cycles show no noticeable changes in diffraction peaks vs pristine, confirming preserved cubic crystal structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 6B shows the XRD patterns of pristine and cycled cathodes at the 50th, 100th, and 250th cycles. There were no noticeable changes in the diffraction peaks upon repeated insertion and extraction of the guest ions.
